extracted.intended_audience: students/readers of classical algebra/geometry (Italian-language historical text)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and operational rules for binomials, quadrinomials, and related line/surface types (medial, bimedial, major/minor lines), plus rules for multiplying such expressions and conditions under which roots/products are rational or medial. Extracts classical geometric‑algebraic criteria and multiplication procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — linea mediale / superficie mediale
rubrics_metrics.description: A line is called 'mediale' (median) when it produces a medial surface; a surface is called medial when the two generating lines relate so that the surface formed is of 'mediale' nature (i.e., corresponds to a medial magnitude rather than a rational one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text repeatedly: 'Diciturq5 fuperficies medialio' and 'Diciturq5 linea medialio'; the page explains mediality arises from the relationship of two lines and that medial surfaces/lines are distinguished from rational ones (examples and symbolic instances interspersed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — linea magiore / linea minore (major/minor line)
rubrics_metrics.description: A line may be called 'magio2e' (maggiore, major) or 'mino2e' (minore, minor) relative to another; the pair form compositions where the major and minor components determine how sums/differences and medial relations occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains when one line is considered the greater or lesser in a composition, how such names affect the naming of composite lines (e.g. when composing two lines the resulting line may be named after the major component) and how these interact in algebraic constructions and multiplicative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — linea bimediale / bimedial composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'bimediale' (bimedial) line arises when two lines produce medial surfaces in relation to one another; the bimedial composition is a specific compound of two medial-type lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page uses the term 'bimediale' and contrasts it with monomedial and other compound medialities; it identifies when two component lines yield a bimedial composite and gives notation/examples (several illustrative combinations are listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — primo binomio / secondo / terzo / quarto binomio (classification of binomials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binomials are classified (first, second, third, fourth binomial) according to the nature of their two component lines (rational, medial, greater/lesser, commensurable relations). Each numbered binomial has a distinct defining condition based on those component properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Throughout the text the author states 'primo binomio', 'secondo binomio', 'terco binomio', 'qrto binomio' and gives characteristic properties and examples (e.g. which squares/terms are required, how they relate to the quadrato del numero etc.). Specific numeric examples and symbolic forms are interleaved in the exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — quadrinomio / linea quadrinomia (quadrinomial and quadrinomial line)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quadrinomial (quadrinomio) or quadrinomial line ('linea quadrinomia') is the composition obtained when multiplying binomials (or combining four component terms); its components and structure follow from the squares of components and double products of the parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explains how quadrinomials arise from products of binomials (e.g. 'lo quadrato de la p?ima ... la quarta oel fecódo') and indicates the composition rules: squares of each part and twice the products appear in the expanded form; examples and symbolic numeric illustrations are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule — multiplication of binomials/quadrinomials: squares and double products
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiplying binomials/quadrinomials, form the squares of the individual component lines and include twice the product of each pair of components where required; the quadrinomial components are those squares together with the double products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit passages: 'KnccbùiomìalitqucUa quadrinomialcrcomponentitcon lo doppio de la mulo'plicatibne de una delfe in.laltra' and numerous worked examples (symbolic expansions, numeric instances like '4o.p.*^.52o.fara...') illustrate the rule and show how to collect terms in the product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — when product of one line 'in' another yields rational vs medial numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The product (multiplication) of one line into another yields rational or medial results depending on the proportional/square relations of the component lines: under certain proportional conditions the product is rational, in others it is medial (i.e., a 'radice' rational or mediale emerges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases such as 'la multiplicatióe de vna in laltra tic roalc fi corno lepditte' and discussion of when 'radici vniucrfali' or 'mediale' roots are obtained give rules: check the squares of components and their proportion to determine whether the resulting root/product is rational or medial; worked numeric examples are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition/criterion — 'potentialiter incommensurabiles' (potentially incommensurable lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two lines are called 'potentialiter incommensurabiles' when, in certain constructions, they are not commensurable yet their generated medial surfaces or quadrates admit particular equalities (e.g. both squares accepted as medial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text uses 'potentiter ìcómcnfurabiles' and links this notion to when line pairs produce medial surfaces that can be treated in algebraic multiplication; the passage describes conditions for potential incommensurability and consequences for composing binomials/quadrinomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction/procedure — method to multiply expressions with irrational (medial) roots by converting to squares and pairing
rubrics_metrics.description: To multiply expressions containing irrational (medial) components, proceed by taking the squares of the relevant lines, arranging terms so that squares of one are multiplied into squares of another, and then account for the double products; this reduces the operation to manipulation of squares and known rational/medial pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text repeatedly instructs converting to squares (e.g. 'multiplicare el quadrato oc luna in lo quadrato oe laltra') and then performing multiplications of those squares and summing double products; examples illustrate the step-by-step reduction and recombination (numeric symbolic sequences appear throughout).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — naming/composition rule when composing multiple lines (how to name resulting composite)
rubrics_metrics.description: When composing lines (e.g. adding or connecting components) the name of the resulting composite often follows the major component (line named after the maggiore); special naming rules apply when multiple components are linked or when lines are in specific medial/rational relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages like 'la ql cofa tomo tal piare coli dicido... la quale dicemo' and examples showing when a composite line is called by the name of its major part explain the naming convention; the text gives examples of when the composite is called 'linea magio:e' and when alternative names apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — when two compound lines yield the same medial surface (acceptability for composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two compound lines (assemblies of component lines) may be considered acceptable for forming a medial surface if both their squares are equally accepted as medial and the medial surface formed is common — this is a necessary condition to regard their composition as yielding medial roots or to proceed with multiplicative constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement 'quarum ambo quadrata pariter accepta fint mediale' and subsequent discussion indicate that equality of medial acceptance of component squares is a prerequisite to treat the compound as producing a shared medial surface; used as test when establishing potential incommensurability and further multiplicative steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion — decomposition rule: to handle difficult multiplications break components into modules of the same type
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiplication involves many interleaved irrational roots (difficult multiplications), decompose the binomial/quadrinomial into modules (parts) of similar form so that each module can be multiplied according to the standard rule of squares and double products, then recombine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text notes difficulty: 'H per che in la p:arica e difficile tal multiplicare per efferui mifte radici imiuer fali...' and recommends multiplying in parts or following a 'ferma regola' — i.e., handle squares and double products systematically, with worked examples showing partial multiplications and recombination.
